title_en: Japan's 2026 Antarctic environmental-emergency reform: tourism, shipping and Annex VI

quick_take.what_changed: Act No. 36 of 2026 expanded advance procedures for certain Antarctic sea-only activities in June; separate emergency-response and cost-liability provisions depend on Annex VI's entry into force.
quick_take.who_is_affected: Organizers and participants in Antarctic tourism or scientific voyages, including activities without a continental landing, may face different Japanese procedures.
quick_take.what_to_do_now: Check whether a Japanese confirmation application or advance notification applies now, and distinguish it from the Annex VI-dependent emergency obligations.

instruments.name_en: 2026 amendment to the Antarctic Environmental Protection Act

watch_pages.label: Ministry of the Environment Antarctic legislation
Ministry of the Environment press releases

paragraphs: Antarctic tourism and vessel activity have expanded, increasing concern about fuel spills and other environmental emergencies in a remote ecosystem where response capacity is limited. The Ministry of the Environment identified a gap between existing activity controls and a comprehensive liability framework for preventing and responding to emergencies.

Annex VI to the Protocol on Environmental Protection to the Antarctic Treaty was adopted in 2005 but requires acceptance by the original consultative parties before taking effect. Japan's 2026 legislation was designed both to close a domestic coverage gap for sea-only activity and to prepare the legal duties needed for Japan to implement the Annex when it becomes effective.

Following deliberation by the Central Environment Council, the Ministry received its recommendation on 13 March 2026. The Cabinet approved the bill on 3 April, the Diet enacted it on 2 June, and Act No. 36 was promulgated on 10 June.

From 30 June 2026, certain Antarctic tourism and scientific activities conducted only at sea became subject to Japanese confirmation procedures; the Ministry also explained advance notification for participation in activities run by foreign organizers. The separate emergency-plan, response and cost-liability framework is tied to Annex VI becoming effective for Japan, rather than automatically commencing with the June procedural changes.

An October 2026 consultation on protected-area management-plan changes arose from the Antarctic Treaty meeting; it is a separate subordinate-rule process and must not be mistaken for commencement of the Annex VI liability regime.

confirmed.text: Advance procedures for the newly covered sea-only activities have applied since 30 June 2026.

expected: The Annex VI-dependent provisions will commence according to the statutory commencement mechanism once the relevant treaty conditions are fulfilled; the date cannot be inferred from the earlier procedural commencement.
uncertainties: A confirmed effective date for the main Annex VI emergency-liability provisions was not established in the primary materials checked.
Whether a particular foreign-organized voyage requires confirmation or notification depends on the operator and participant arrangements.

paragraphs: Antarctic cruise and research operators should treat the June 2026 procedural expansion as an existing compliance issue, even for voyages without a landing. For Japanese participants in foreign-organized activities, the Ministry identifies a distinct advance notification route.

The later emergency-response framework would affect preparedness and potential cost allocation following an environmental emergency. Businesses should not treat those future duties as already in force merely because part of the 2026 amendment has commenced.
checklist: Classify the proposed voyage by organizer, activity and whether it involves landing, then check confirmation versus notification requirements.
Document emergency-prevention and response arrangements in preparation for any later Annex VI-dependent provisions.
Monitor the Ministry's Antarctic-law page and treaty developments for the legally effective commencement date.
